closingKeywordReason: #1290: all three remainder items ($ref targets, global security, trace) reproduced red on origin/main 33139d86 and are fixed with planted-positive tests (path-item parameters were fixed in #1607). #1503: S1 (body-read network errors classified; GET retried, writes never re-sent), S2 (AbortError rethrown unchanged test) and S3 ('may not have been posted' wording) all landed.
assumptions: #1290: a $ref is resolved only when it is a local '#/...' JSON pointer; external, unresolvable and cyclic refs are compared as written (a recursive schema terminates).
#1290: sibling keys next to a resolved $ref are kept and merged over the resolved target (OAS 3.1 allows summary/description siblings).
#1290: an operation's explicit security (including []) overrides top-level security; moving an identical requirement from global to the operation is not a change.
#1290: ref resolution is not memoized; a pathological spec with deeply nested repeated refs grows exponentially. Accepted for realistic specs.
#1503: a body-read network error is retried on GET only (per human fork); PATCH and POST are not re-sent for it but now surface as GitHubNetworkError so the sticky upsert degrades.
#1503: fetchWithRetry was replaced by readWithRetry(url, init, sleep, consume) rather than kept beside it, so no export is left unused.
#1503: the shared network-error notice now says 'may not have been posted' for every method (a GET lookup failure is also accurately described by it).
